name: zmath_line_vs_sphere_hit
description: zMath::LineVsSphereHit tests a ray-like line segment direction against a sphere and writes the inward hit normal.
known_limits: No isolated VC COFF byte comparison is recorded for this helper; tier S verification is deferred to a coherent zMath geometry/vector source-cluster pass.
The source preserves the recovered fast square-root bit estimate and stable quadratic root selection rather than replacing it with the standard sqrt function.
functional_evidence: Binary Ninja assembly for 0x475210 validates ECX as segA, EDX as segB, radius as the first stack argument, sphereCenterRelSegB as the second stack argument, outInwardNormal as the third stack argument, lineDelta = segA - segB, zero-length rejection, center dot and center-distance-minus-radius quadratic terms, discriminant rejection, the recovered fast square-root bit estimate, special handling when the origin is exactly on the sphere, inward-normal write as sphereCenterRelSegB - hitScale * lineDelta, and zMath::Vec3Normalize on the output before returning 1.

The native zMath smoke verifies a forward hit writes an inward normal, the exact-on-sphere branch hits, behind-origin and zero-length lines reject without clobbering the output, and a beside-sphere miss returns 0.
